overall_reason: A 'Welcome' page with a developer 'Debug mode' toggle above 24 identical placeholder rows ('Acme Corp', 'Paid', '$420.00'): filler data nobody chose, presented with no summary, sort, filter or signal of what needs attention.

findings.evidence: Every row is 'Acme Corp / Paid / $420.00'; only the number changes and dates cycle 2026-03-01..09 three times, so Invoice 1009 (2026-03-01) is dated before Invoice 1008 (2026-03-09). Failed T-FILLER: the data is not real and the table cannot be read for anything (no unpaid, no different customer, no outlier).
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real or realistic invoice records with varied customers, statuses and amounts]; dates monotonic with invoice numbers
findings.why: Placeholder residue at ship; identical rows hide every design problem the real list will have.

findings.evidence: A developer toggle sits as the first control on the page, above the content; T-DELETION: removing it loses nothing for the user.
findings.after: Remove from the user-facing page (move behind a dev flag)
findings.why: Development controls left in the UI read as unfinished output.

findings.evidence: T-FIVE-SECOND: 'Welcome' says nothing about the page (an invoice list), who it is for or what to do; T-FRESH-READER lists it as a line that fits any app.
findings.after: Invoices, with a one-line summary (e.g. 'n unpaid, $x due this week') [DATA NEEDED: real totals]
findings.why: Each page gets one job and its heading should name it.

findings.evidence: Status is plain grey text identical for all rows and Amount is left-aligned prose-style, so nothing in the list can be scanned for state or size; the 'Date' column is clipped at the container edge even at 1440 (table 768px inside a 695px box).
findings.before: Left-aligned amounts, status as plain text, clipped date column
findings.after: Right-align amounts with tabular figures, show status as a labelled badge only when not 'Paid', widen the container or drop the redundant 'Invoice' prefix so all columns fit at desktop
findings.why: A list's design job is scanning; nothing here differentiates rows.

strengths: Uses a real <table> with a caption and a named, focusable horizontal scroll region; spacing and type tokens are consistent.
not_investigated: Behaviour of the 'Debug mode' toggle (no live interaction).
